review: 506.1-2: base variant carried a delta and the setup step (declare_blockers) came after the attack decision; base attacker fixed in decisions, step set to beginning_of_combat, variant delta names the swap.

506.3a-1: the does_not_fire variant changed three facts (no animation, different attacker, different target); both creatures now attack and the only delta is the trigger's target, with life totals recomputed (16 vs 15).

506.3d-1: no does_not_fire variant (the second variant only skipped ninjutsu), and A's draw from an empty library would lose the game; added Ainok Strike Leader whose Goblin token enters attacking in the declare attackers step, the delta is B blocking that token, A declines the draw and has a library.

506.3c: skip reason was false (ninjutsu enters attacking the returned creature's planeswalker, which can die in response); removed the skip and added scenario 506.3c-1 with Jace Beleren killed by Lightning Bolt in response to ninjutsu.
506.4-1: base variant carried a delta and the setup step came after the attack; attacker fixed in decisions, step set to beginning_of_combat, Shock timed in the declare blockers step.
506.4-2: base variant carried a delta ('A does not respond'); moved into the decisions, setup step set before the attack.
506.4-3: base variant carried a delta; the activation moved into the decisions, setup step set before the attack.
506.4-4: base variant carried a delta; target fixed in the decisions, setup step set before the attack.
506.4-5: base variant carried a delta; the Disenchant cast moved into the decisions, setup step set before the attack.
506.4a-1: base variant carried a delta; cast timing fixed in the decisions.
506.4a-2: base variant carried a delta; cast timing fixed in the decisions.
506.4b-1: base variant carried a delta; cast timing fixed in the decisions.
506.4b-2: base variant carried a delta; cast timing fixed in the decisions.
506.4c-1: base variant carried a delta and the Bolt's timing was unstated; Bolt fixed in the declare attackers step and no-block fixed in the decisions, so each variant changes one fact.
506.8a-1: base decisions left the attack to the variants; base attack and query step fixed so each variant changes one fact.

skipped.reason: cannot occur in a two-player Forge game: the attacking player is always the active player, and no card Forge implements puts a creature onto the battlefield attacking under another player's control (every put-attacking effect, such as Zara, Chorale of the Void or Noctis, puts it under the attacker's or its owner's control on the owner's own attack)

cannot occur in a two-player Forge game: the effects that put a creature onto the battlefield blocking (Flash Foliage, Mirror Match, Brimaz) are controlled by the defending player and name attackers that attack that player or their planeswalker, so the exception for an attacker not attacking the entering creature's controller never arises

cannot be illustrated: it needs a battle that is also a creature put onto the battlefield attacking or blocking, and no card Forge implements both gives a battle the creature type and puts permanents onto the battlefield attacking or blocking
cannot be illustrated: it needs a resolving spell or ability that makes a battle an attacking or blocking creature, and no card Forge implements does that

cannot be illustrated: it needs a permanent that is both a creature and a planeswalker blocking an attacker on the opponent's turn, and every planeswalker animation Forge implements (Gideon Jura, Gideon Blackblade and similar) lasts only on its controller's own turn
cannot be illustrated: it needs an attacked permanent that is both a planeswalker and a battle, and no card Forge implements makes a permanent both

scenarios.title: Declare blockers and combat damage steps are skipped when no creature is declared as an attacker

setup.notes: Fog Patch can be cast only during the declare blockers step, so a legal cast shows that the step exists. B has no creatures.

decisions: Both players pass priority in the beginning of combat step.
A declares no attackers.
B holds priority windows only in the steps the combat phase actually has; B casts nothing.

variants.label: no_attackers
variants.expected: No declare blockers step and no combat damage step take place. At no priority B receives in this combat is casting Fog Patch legal (can_play false at declare attackers and at end of combat). B's life stays 20.

variants.label: one_attacker
variants.delta: A declares Grizzly Bears as an attacker against B.
variants.expected: The declare blockers step takes place and B receives priority in it: casting Fog Patch (tapping both Forests) is legal there. B casts nothing, declares no blockers, and takes 2 combat damage in the combat damage step: B's life is 18.

scenarios.forge_notes: If Forge does not stop at the declare attackers step at all when nobody attacks, the playability verdict at that step is simply absent rather than false.

scenarios.title: A first strike attacker causes a second combat damage step

setup.notes: Youthful Knight is 2/1 with first strike; Elite Vanguard is a vanilla 2/1.

decisions: A attacks B with Youthful Knight.
B blocks Youthful Knight with Grizzly Bears.
No spells or abilities are used; combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: first_strike_attacker
variants.expected: Two combat damage steps take place. In the first-strike step Youthful Knight deals 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, which is destroyed and goes to B's graveyard. In the regular step Grizzly Bears is gone and deals no damage: Youthful Knight has no damage marked and stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: plain_attacker
variants.delta: A attacks with Elite Vanguard (no first strike) instead of Youthful Knight, and B blocks it with Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Only one combat damage step takes place. Elite Vanguard and Grizzly Bears deal 2 damage to each other at the same time; both are destroyed and go to their owners' graveyards.

scenarios.title: A noncreature permanent is not offered as an attacker until it becomes a creature

setup.notes: Treetop Village has been under A's control since before the turn began.

decisions: A moves to combat; at the declare attackers step A's legal attackers are queried.

variants.label: land_not_animated
variants.expected: Legal attackers for A: Grizzly Bears only. Treetop Village is a land and not a creature, so declaring it as an attacker is illegal.

variants.label: land_animated
variants.delta: In main1 A activates Treetop Village ({1}{G}, tapping both Forests); the ability resolves and Treetop Village is a 3/3 green Ape creature with trample until end of turn.
variants.expected: Legal attackers for A: Grizzly Bears and Treetop Village.

scenarios.title: A noncreature permanent is not offered as a blocker until it becomes a creature
decisions: A attacks B with Hill Giant.
B's legal blockers are queried.

variants.label: land_not_animated
variants.expected: Legal blockers for B: Grizzly Bears only. Treetop Village and Mountain are lands and not creatures, so they cannot be declared as blockers.

variants.label: land_animated
variants.delta: In the declare attackers step B activates Treetop Village ({1}{G}, tapping both Forests); it resolves and Treetop Village is a 3/3 creature until end of turn.
variants.expected: Legal blockers for B: Grizzly Bears and Treetop Village. Mountain is still not offered.

scenarios.title: Only players, planeswalkers and battles can be attacked; a creature cannot
decisions: A moves to combat; at the declare attackers step the legal attack targets for Hill Giant are queried.

variants.label: jace_present
variants.expected: Attacking Grizzly Bears is illegal: a creature is not an attack target. The legal attack targets for Hill Giant are player B and Jace Beleren.

variants.label: jace_candidate
variants.delta: The attack target queried is Jace Beleren instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Attacking Jace Beleren is legal: a planeswalker can be attacked.

variants.label: jace_killed
variants.delta: In main1 A casts Lightning Bolt targeting Jace Beleren, tapping Mountain; it resolves and Jace Beleren (loyalty 3) goes to B's graveyard.
variants.expected: Legal attack targets for Hill Giant: player B only. Grizzly Bears is still not an attack target.

scenarios.title: A noncreature permanent put onto the battlefield attacking enters but is not an attacker

setup.notes: Echoing Assault: whenever A attacks a player, create a 1/1 token copy of a target nontoken creature attacking that player, tapped and attacking, sacrificed at the next end step.

decisions: A taps Mountain to pay {1} and activates Mutavault; it resolves and Mutavault is a 2/2 creature land until end of turn.
A attacks B with Mutavault and Grizzly Bears.
Echoing Assault triggers and A targets Mutavault; B has no responses.
The trigger resolves. B declares no blockers (B has no creatures); combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: copies_animated_land
variants.expected: The token copy of Mutavault is a land and not a creature (the animation is not copied): it enters the battlefield tapped but is not an attacking permanent and deals no combat damage. Mutavault and Grizzly Bears each deal 2 combat damage: B's life is 16. The token is sacrificed at the next end step.

variants.label: copies_creature
variants.delta: Echoing Assault's trigger targets Grizzly Bears instead of Mutavault.
variants.expected: The token copy of Grizzly Bears is a 1/1 creature that enters tapped and attacking B. Mutavault deals 2, Grizzly Bears 2 and the token 1: B's life is 15. The token is sacrificed at the next end step.

scenarios.forge_notes: Echoing Assault copies via CopyPermanent with TokenAttacking$ TriggeredAttackedTarget; whether Forge leaves a non-creature token in the attackers list is the thing to check.

scenarios.title: A creature put onto the battlefield attacking a planeswalker that has left the battlefield enters but is not attacking

setup.notes: B has no creatures. Ninjutsu puts the Ninja onto the battlefield attacking the same player or planeswalker the returned creature was attacking (702.49c).

decisions: A attacks Jace Beleren with Grizzly Bears.
B declares no blockers.
In the declare blockers step A activates ninjutsu of Ninja of the Deep Hours ({1}{U}, tapping both Islands), returning the unblocked Grizzly Bears to hand.
In response B casts Lightning Bolt targeting Jace Beleren, tapping Mountain; it resolves and Jace Beleren (loyalty 3) goes to B's graveyard.
The ninjutsu ability resolves; combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: planeswalker_gone
variants.expected: Ninja of the Deep Hours enters the battlefield tapped but is not an attacking creature: it deals no combat damage. B's life is 20. Jace Beleren is in B's graveyard and Grizzly Bears is in A's hand.

variants.label: planeswalker_stays
variants.delta: B does not cast Lightning Bolt.
variants.expected: Ninja of the Deep Hours enters tapped and attacking Jace Beleren, unblocked, and deals 2 combat damage to it: Jace Beleren's loyalty is 1. Its draw trigger does not fire (no damage to a player). B's life is 20.

scenarios.forge_notes: Whether Forge's ninjutsu resolution checks the stored defender and leaves the Ninja out of combat when that planeswalker is gone is the thing to check.

scenarios.title: A creature put onto the battlefield attacking during the declare blockers step enters unblocked; one put attacking during the declare attackers step can be blocked

setup.notes: Ainok Strike Leader (2/2): when A attacks with it, A creates a 1/1 red Goblin creature token tapped and attacking B. Ninja of the Deep Hours: 2/2, ninjutsu {1}{U}.

decisions: A attacks B with Ainok Strike Leader. Its trigger resolves in the declare attackers step: a 1/1 Goblin token enters tapped and attacking B.
B declares no blockers.
In the declare blockers step A activates ninjutsu of Ninja of the Deep Hours ({1}{U}, tapping both Islands), returning the unblocked Ainok Strike Leader to hand; the ability resolves.
Combat damage is dealt; A declines the optional draw from Ninja of the Deep Hours' trigger.

variants.label: no_blocks
variants.expected: Ninja of the Deep Hours enters tapped and attacking B as an unblocked creature; no blocker was or can be declared for it. The Goblin token is unblocked. Ninja deals 2 and the token 1 combat damage to B: B's life is 17. Ainok Strike Leader is in A's hand.

variants.label: token_blocked
variants.delta: B declares Grizzly Bears as a blocker of the Goblin token.
variants.expected: The block is legal: the Goblin token entered attacking during the declare attackers step, before blockers were declared, so it is blocked. Grizzly Bears deals 2 damage to the token, which is destroyed; the token deals 1 damage to Grizzly Bears. Ninja of the Deep Hours still enters unblocked and deals 2 combat damage to B: B's life is 18.

scenarios.forge_notes: No Forge card puts a creature onto the battlefield attacking at a step of the controller's choosing, so the contrast uses two effects of the same combat: a token put attacking in the declare attackers step (blockable) next to a ninjutsu creature put attacking in the declare blockers step (unblocked).

scenarios.title: A creature that leaves the battlefield is removed from combat
decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B blocks it with B's Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B casts Shock targeting the attacker, tapping Mountain; A does not respond; Shock resolves.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: attacker_dies
variants.expected: A's Grizzly Bears takes 2 damage, is destroyed and leaves the battlefield, so it is removed from combat. B's Grizzly Bears is no longer blocking anything, deals and takes no combat damage and has no damage marked.

variants.label: attacker_survives
variants.delta: A attacks with Earth Elemental instead of Grizzly Bears (B blocks it and Shocks it the same way).
variants.expected: Earth Elemental takes 2 damage from Shock and stays on the battlefield and in combat. It deals 4 combat damage to B's Grizzly Bears, which is destroyed, and takes 2 combat damage from it: Earth Elemental has 4 damage marked and survives.

scenarios.title: A creature whose controller changes is removed from combat
decisions: A attacks B with Hill Giant.
B blocks with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B casts Act of Aggression targeting Hill Giant, tapping five Mountains.
A does not respond; Act of Aggression resolves.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: control_changes
variants.expected: B gains control of Hill Giant, which untaps and gains haste until end of turn, and it is removed from combat: it deals no combat damage and B's Grizzly Bears takes no damage. Both players are at 20. Hill Giant returns to A's control at end of turn.

variants.label: target_illegal
variants.delta: In response to Act of Aggression A casts Gods Willing targeting Hill Giant, tapping Plains, choosing protection from red and scrying 1 with an empty library; it resolves first.
variants.expected: Act of Aggression's only target is illegal when it tries to resolve, so it fizzles and A keeps control. Hill Giant stays in combat, blocked: it deals 3 damage to Grizzly Bears, which is destroyed, and takes 2 damage. Both players are at 20.

scenarios.title: An attacking or blocking creature that regenerates is removed from combat

setup.notes: Battle Hurda is a 3/3 with first strike. Gorilla Chieftain is a 3/3 with {1}{G}: Regenerate.

decisions: A attacks B with Battle Hurda.
B blocks with Gorilla Chieftain.
In the declare blockers step B activates Gorilla Chieftain's regeneration ability ({1}{G}, tapping both Forests); it resolves, creating a regeneration shield.
Combat damage is dealt (first-strike step, then regular step).

variants.label: regenerates
variants.expected: In the first-strike step Battle Hurda deals 3 damage to Gorilla Chieftain; it is destroyed, so the shield is used instead: it is tapped, its damage is removed, and it is removed from combat. In the regular step it deals no damage: Battle Hurda has no damage marked. Gorilla Chieftain stays on the battlefield, tapped.

variants.label: no_shield
variants.delta: B does not activate the regeneration ability.
variants.expected: In the first-strike step Battle Hurda deals 3 damage to Gorilla Chieftain, which is destroyed and goes to B's graveyard before it deals any damage. Battle Hurda has no damage marked.

scenarios.title: A creature that phases out is removed from combat
decisions: A attacks B with Hill Giant only; Elite Vanguard stays home.
B blocks with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B casts Galadriel's Dismissal unkicked ({W}, tapping Plains) targeting Hill Giant; A does not respond; it resolves.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: attacker_phases_out
variants.expected: Hill Giant phases out and is removed from combat. B's Grizzly Bears takes no damage and Hill Giant deals none; both players are at 20. Hill Giant phases back in during A's next untap step.

variants.label: bystander_phases_out
variants.delta: Galadriel's Dismissal targets Elite Vanguard, which is not in combat, instead of Hill Giant.
variants.expected: Elite Vanguard phases out. Hill Giant stays in combat, blocked: it deals 3 damage to Grizzly Bears, which is destroyed, and takes 2 damage. Both players are at 20.

scenarios.title: An attacking creature that stops being a creature is removed from combat

setup.notes: Opalescence makes each other non-Aura enchantment a creature with power and toughness equal to its mana value, so Sylvan Library (mana value 2) is a 2/2 enchantment creature.

decisions: A attacks B with Sylvan Library.
B blocks with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B casts Disenchant ({1}{W}, tapping both Plains) targeting Opalescence; A does not respond; it resolves.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: creature_status_lost
variants.expected: Opalescence is destroyed, Sylvan Library is no longer a creature and is removed from combat. It deals no combat damage and stays on the battlefield; B's Grizzly Bears takes no damage and stays.

scenarios.title: An effect that would have kept a creature from attacking does not remove it once it is declared as an attacker
decisions: A attacks B with Hill Giant.
In the declare attackers step, after Hill Giant is declared as an attacker, B casts Off Balance targeting Hill Giant, tapping Plains; it resolves.
B declares no blockers (B has no creatures); combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: cast_after_declaration
variants.expected: Hill Giant stays an attacking creature although it now can't attack, and deals 3 combat damage to B: B's life is 17.

variants.expected: Hill Giant can't attack this turn and is not declared as an attacker. No combat damage is dealt: B's life is 20.

scenarios.title: An effect that would have kept a creature from blocking does not remove it once it is declared as a blocker
decisions: A attacks B with Hill Giant.
B blocks Hill Giant with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step A casts Off Balance targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Plains; it resolves.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: cast_after_block
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears stays a blocking creature although it now can't block. Hill Giant deals 3 damage to it and it is destroyed; it deals 2 damage to Hill Giant. B's life is 20.

variants.label: cast_before_block
variants.delta: A casts Off Balance in the declare attackers step, before blockers are declared, so B cannot declare Grizzly Bears as a blocker.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears can't block this turn, so B declares no blockers. Hill Giant is unblocked and deals 3 combat damage to B: B's life is 17.

scenarios.title: Tapping a declared blocker does not remove it from combat or stop its combat damage
decisions: A attacks B with Hill Giant.
B blocks Hill Giant with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare blockers step B casts Icy Blast with X=1 ({1}{U}, tapping both Islands) targeting Grizzly Bears; it resolves (no ferocious: B controls no creature with power 4 or greater).
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: tapped_after_block
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears becomes tapped but remains a blocking creature. Combat damage is still dealt: it deals 2 damage to Hill Giant and takes 3, so it is destroyed. B's life is 20.

variants.label: tapped_before_block
variants.delta: B casts Icy Blast in the declare attackers step, before blockers are declared, so tapped Grizzly Bears cannot be declared as a blocker.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is tapped and can't be declared as a blocker. Hill Giant is unblocked and deals 3 combat damage to B: B's life is 17.

variants.expected: Serra Angel is tapped and can't be declared as an attacker. No combat damage is dealt: B's life is 20.

decisions: A attacks Jace Beleren with Hill Giant.

scenarios.title: A spell castable only before attackers are declared cannot be cast once the declare attackers step has begun

setup.notes: Master Warcraft ({2}{R/W}{R/W}) can be cast only before attackers are declared.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare attackers step, A's casting Master Warcraft with the four Mountains is queried.

variants.label: after_declaration
variants.expected: Casting Master Warcraft is illegal (can_play false): the declare attackers step has begun.

variants.label: before_declaration
variants.delta: The query is made in the beginning of combat step, before the declare attackers step begins.
variants.expected: Casting Master Warcraft is legal (can_play true).

variants.label: no_attackers_declared
variants.delta: A declares no attackers (the query is still made in the declare attackers step).
variants.expected: Casting Master Warcraft is illegal (can_play false) even though no attacker was declared: the declare attackers step has begun.

scenarios.title: A spell castable only during combat can be cast in any combat phase of a turn with several

setup.notes: A cast Relentless Assault in main1 this turn, so the turn has an additional combat phase and an additional main phase after main1, followed by the regular combat phase. The step given is the beginning of combat of the regular, second combat phase.

decisions: A's casting Mandate of Peace ({1}{W}, tapping both Plains) is queried.

variants.label: second_combat_phase
variants.expected: Casting Mandate of Peace is legal (can_play true): it is combat, and the spell can be cast in any combat phase of the turn.

variants.label: additional_main_phase
variants.delta: The query is made in the additional main phase between the two combat phases instead of the second combat phase's beginning of combat step.

scenarios.title: A spell castable only before attackers are declared can be cast only before the first combat phase of the turn

setup.notes: A cast Relentless Assault in main1 this turn (paying with the four tapped Mountains), so the turn has an additional combat phase right after main1, an additional main phase, and then the regular combat phase. The step given is the beginning of combat of the regular, second combat phase. Master Warcraft has no 'during combat' wording.

decisions: A's casting Master Warcraft with four untapped Mountains is queried.

variants.label: second_combat_phase
variants.expected: Casting Master Warcraft is illegal (can_play false): the first combat phase of the turn has already passed its declare attackers step.

variants.label: first_combat_phase
variants.delta: The query is made in the beginning of combat step of the additional, first combat phase.
variants.expected: Casting Master Warcraft is legal (can_play true).

scenarios.title: When no attacker is declared, a spell castable only before blockers are declared can be cast only until the declare attackers step ends

setup.notes: A declared no attackers this combat, so the declare blockers and combat damage steps were skipped.

decisions: A declares no attackers.
In the end of combat step, A's casting Gorilla War Cry ({1}{R}, tapping both Mountains) is queried.

variants.label: end_of_combat
variants.expected: Casting Gorilla War Cry is illegal (can_play false): the declare attackers step has ended and no declare blockers step exists to cast it before.

variants.label: declare_attackers_step
variants.delta: The query is made in the declare attackers step, after A declared no attackers, instead of the end of combat step.
variants.expected: Casting Gorilla War Cry is legal (can_play true).

scenarios.forge_notes: Only the first sentence of 506.8e is illustrated. The second sentence (a skipped combat phase leaves casting possible only before the precombat main phase ends) gives the same verdicts as the ordinary 'before attackers are declared' case in every position, so no separate variant tells it apart. If Forge skips the declare attackers step's priority when nobody attacks, the declare_attackers_step verdict is absent.

scenarios.title: A spell castable only during combat after blockers are declared cannot be cast when the declare blockers step is skipped

setup.notes: A declared no attackers this combat, so the declare blockers and combat damage steps were skipped.

decisions: A's casting Chaotic Strike ({1}{R}, tapping both Mountains) targeting Grizzly Bears is queried.

variants.expected: Casting Chaotic Strike is illegal (can_play false) during this combat phase.

variants.label: blockers_step_happens

variants.expected: Casting Chaotic Strike is legal (can_play true).

scenarios.title: A 'during combat' timing restriction applies to an activated ability

setup.notes: Jade Statue: {2}: becomes a 3/6 Golem artifact creature until end of combat. Activate only during combat.

decisions: A's activating Jade Statue ({2}, tapping both Mountains) is queried.

variants.label: main_phase
variants.expected: Activating Jade Statue is illegal (can_play false): it is not combat.

variants.label: beginning_of_combat
variants.delta: The query is made in the beginning of combat step.
variants.expected: Activating Jade Statue is legal (can_play true).
